4 SPECIAL USE PERMIT CONSIDERATIONS 
As stated in Article 20, Section 2002 of the Navajo County Zoning Ordinance, the Navajo County 
Planning & Zoning Commission shall consider certain factors in making its recommendation to the 
Navajo County Board of Supervisors regarding an SUP application. The Applicant has provided 
additional information regarding these factors; this additional information is summarized in Sections 4.1 
through 4.3 below. 
4.1 Compatibility with the Permissible Uses in the Zoning 
District 
The project area is zoned as RU-20. Under Section 402 of Article 4 in the Navajo County Zoning 
Ordinance, electric power generating plants and facilities such as the proposed project are permitted 
special use within the RU-20 zone.  
The Applicant will comply with the height regulations (Section 404), yard regulations (Section 405), 
intensity of use regulations (Section 406), and parking regulations (Article 25) of the RU-20 zone. 
Specifically, the Applicant will ensure the project design adheres to the following: 
• The project building heights will not exceed either 30 feet or 2 stories and a basement. 
• The project front yard will have a depth of at least 20 feet. For through lots, a front yard will be 
provided along both front lot lines. The yard along each street side of corner lots will conform 
with the applicable front yard regulations. 
• The project side yard on each side of a building will have a width of at least 30 feet. 
• The project rear yard will have a depth of at least 20 feet. 
• The project buildings on the same lot will have a minimum distance of 5 feet between buildings. 
• The project will include an O&M building. According to the parking regulations in Section 2510, 
the project must include one parking space for every three employees on the largest working shift,

<!-- page 823 -->
Draft Special Use Permit Application Red Hills Solar and Storage Project 
 10 August 2024 
or one parking space for every 1,000 square feet of floor area, or fraction thereof, in the building, 
whichever is greater. 
4.2 The Current and Likely Future Uses of Property in the 
Vicinity of the Proposed Use 
Most of the project area and the adjacent properties are vacant, undeveloped high-desert land that are used 
primarily for grazing. Nearby developments include the Apache Railroad and SR 77 to the east; the 
Poseidon Wind Project (formerly the Dry Lake Wind Project) to the north, south, and east; and the 
Smithfield Feed Mill and Hog Farm to the north. The ASLD-administered lands surrounding most of the 
project area are part of the Sugarloaf and Six Mile Draw grazing allotments and are currently leased to 
Gerald Flake (ASLD 2024). The ASLD-administered land north of the project area is currently leased to 
Legacy Ranches LLC in the Ten Mile Cedars grazing allotment and to Glen Flake and Sanford Flake in 
the Divide grazing allotment (ASLD 2024). Finally, one ASLD-administered parcel south of the project 
area is leased to Steven Flake in the Ten Mile Cedars grazing allotment. There are several linear ROWs 
that cross these parcels, including long-term and 10-year ROWs for Poseidon Wind and perpetual ROWs 
for SRP (ASLD 2024). The ASLD parcels surrounding the project area also have oil and gas permits 
associated with HB2 Origination, Inc., Helium-4, Inc., Myriad Resources LLC, and Wolcott, LLC (ASLD 
2024). There are no other known current or future land uses on the Arizona State Trust lands surrounding 
the project area.  
BLM-administered land surrounding the project area is also located within two grazing allotments (“The 
Divide” and “Bar A,” administered by the Safford Field Office) (BLM 2024). ROWs that cross the BLM-
administered land surrounding the project include a Wind Energy Grant for Avangrid Renewables LLC, 
road ROWs for the Poseidon Wind Project and SR 77, an SRP transmission line, Arizona Public Service 
roads, a water facility associated with PFFJ LLC, and the Apache Railroad (BLM 2024). There are no 
other known current or existing future land uses on the federal lands surrounding the project area. 
The Navajo County Comprehensive Use Plan designates all the project area as Rural Edge. The project is 
consistent with Section 2.2, Land Use Element, of the Comprehensive Plan, which states that the land use 
planning should “include consideration of air quality and access to incident solar and wind energy for all 
character areas” (Navajo County 2023:5). Additionally, the Navajo County Board of Supervisors has 
approved a similar type of future land use in the surrounding area (i.e., the Poseidon Wind Project). 
Therefore, the project is compatible with the current and future land uses for the property.  
The Aztec Area Plan designates approximately 1,640 acres of the project area as Rural Edge, which is 
located within Planning Area G (Apache District). Approximately 3,910 acres of the project area are 
designated as Community Village, which is located within Planning Area C (Snowflake North) (see 
Appendix C). The purpose of the Aztec Rural Edge character area is to “provide lower density 
developments adjacent to Community Village areas or primary transportation corridors” (Aztec Land and 
Cattle Company Limited 2011:20). Rural Edge character areas also encourage development of “utilities 
and energy generation facilities” (Aztec Land and Cattle Company Limited 2011:20). Planning Area G is 
traversed by power lines and has good highway access to SR 77 and SR 377. The project is a utility-scale 
solar energy generation facility that would add additional power lines to the landscape along SR 77. The 
project would be compatible with the Rural Edge character area in Planning Area G.  
The Community Village character areas are intended to “provide large areas with higher density 
residential development with a mix of related commercial, employment, industrial, institutional and 
recreational uses extending from highway corridors, highway intersections, future major roadways and 
existing communities in a more urban setting” (Aztec Land and Cattle Company Limited 2011:20).

<!-- page 824 -->
Draft Special Use Permit Application Red Hills Solar and Storage Project 
 11 August 2024 
Planning Area C is a planned extension of the urban development pattern within the Snowflake, Arizona. 
Anticipated development in this area is a “mixed use mater planned community with a variety of uses, 
including residential, commercial, employment, recreational, and other urban-related uses” (Aztec Land 
and Cattle Company Limited 2011:32). “It is anticipated that between 4,500 and 8,900 homes may be 
built within this district, and a significant amount of non-residential land uses to support the population of 
the entire area, including the areas around Snowflake and Taylor” (Aztec Land and Cattle Company 
Limited 2011:32). The project would enhance energy supplies in Arizona, thereby supporting the 
population as a non-residential land use. Therefore, the project is compatible with the Community Village 
character area in Planning Area C.  
4.3 The Effects of the Proposed Use on Public Health, 
Safety, and General Welfare 
The Applicant has considered the project’s impact to public health, safety, and general welfare by 
describing potential fire protection measures (see Section 3.1.4.2) and will minimize impacts to the 
general public’s health and safety through application of an SSSP (see Section 3.1.4.3). The Applicant has 
also performed environmental due diligence to avoid and minimize impacts to the biological, cultural, 
aquatic, and visual resources in the project area, which are being submitted with this request.

Mr. Cooper,  
I am writing to formally request a waiver for the Neighborhood Community Meeting requirement in 
connection with our Special Use Permit proposal for the Red Hills Solar Project located at Navajo County 
Assessor Parcel Numbers: 202- 27-003F, 202-27-003L, 202- 27-003J, 202- 50-002, 202- 50-003, 202- 50-

According to Navajo County’s code provision in Section 2907, "An applicant may make a written request 
and receive a written determination whether, due to impractical circumstances, such as a site surrounded 
by State or federal lands, the requirement for a Neighborhood Community Meeting may be waived by the 
Director, or their designee. This request must explain why the applicant’s Citizen Review Plan provides 
other adequate, alternative opportunities for citizens to express any concerns, problems, or issues they 
may have with the proposal in advance of the public hearing." 
Our site is uniquely positioned in that it is predominantly surrounded by federal and state lands, with only 
three neighboring parcels  which are privately owned  that are not party to this application and could 
potentially be impacted by our proposal. None of these parcels have residential homes on them. Given 
this context, we believe that hosting a Neighborhood Community Meeting would be impractical and 
unnecessary. 
To ensure that all potentially affected property owners  have adequate opportunities to express any 
concerns or issues, we propose the following alternative:  
Direct Mail Notifications: We will send detailed project information, including a comprehensive 
description of the proposal, to the property owners  within 300 feet of the  project site. This will 
include contact information for a project representative who can answer questions and address 
concerns directly. A draft copy of the letter is attached with this request.   
We are confident that these measures will provide ample opportunity for property owners’ input and 
effectively address any potential concerns. We are committed to transparency and open communication 
throughout the planning process.

The Stellar Red Hills Solar 
and Storage Project 
(project) 
Site
-
Specific Safety Plan (SSSP
 
or “the plan”
) 
outlines 
the necessary actions to safeguard 
project 
employees, emergency responders, and the local community in 
case of an 
emergenc
y
. It includes crucial contact details for emergency personnel and delineates procedures 
for preventing, mitigating, and addressing incidents effectively.
 
This plan aims to define the response actions for personnel at the 
project 
during emergencies, prioritizing 
health and safety for both workers and nearby residents while minimizing environmental damage. As a 
dynamic document, it will undergo regular updates to enhance threat detection and response efficiency. 
Further, 
the 
project is committed to revising the plan as required or deemed necessary by County staff. 
This 
SSSP
 
is relevant to all employees, contractors, vendors, and visitors at the 
project
.
 
A log for visitor and contractor check
-
ins and check
-
outs will be maintained to ensure everyone is accounted 
for in an emergency. All personnel should carry a photo ID for quick identification during accidents or medical 
situations, with site management po
tentially requiring names on hard hats 
as well
.
 
1.1
 
Pr
o
je
c
t
 
D
e
scri
p
t
i
o
n
 
Stellar Red Hills Solar LLC
 
(Stellar)
 
is 
constructing
 
the project, which is 
a
 
1,000
-
megawatt (MW) utility
-
scale 
photovoltaic (PV) solar energy generation facility and a 
4
,000
-
MW
h
 
battery energy storage system (BESS). The 
project is located on approximately 9,
09
0 acres of privately owned land and 123 acres of Arizona State Trust 
Land administered by the Arizona State Land Department (ASLD) in unincorporated Navajo County, Arizona, 
3.5 miles north of Snowflake
 
(the project area)
.
 
The project includes 
a 
920
-
foot
 
long, 500
-
kilovolt (kV) generation intertie transmission (gen
-
tie) line from the 
on
-
site substation to the proposed point of interconnection at the existing Salt River Project (SRP) Sugarloaf 
Substation, located in the project area. The project would also 
include an operations and maintenance (O&M) 
building and other ancillary facilities. 
 
The project will help Salt River Project (SRP) meet its peak electrical load requirements and, by doing so, will 
lessen the need to dispatch less efficient, non
-
renewable “peaking resources,” such as natural gas
-
fired 
generating stations. In addition, the 
project will facilitate the further integration of intermittent (e.g., solar and 
wind energy) generating resources. The project will also bring numerous jobs to Navajo County during 
construction
,
 
decommissioning,
 
and 
for 
operation and 
maintenance
 
(O&M)
 
while generating tax revenues to 
support local schools, hospitals, and other beneficiaries throughout the 
anticipated 
35
-
year  life of the project.

.3
 
Spill Prevention
 
The following general requirements for any hazardous substances stored or used at this facility
:
 
•
 
Ensure all hazardous substances are properly labeled and tightly sealed.
 
•
 
Maintain and review 
MSDS
 
for hazardous materials.
 
•
 
Store, dispense, and/or use hazardous substances in a way that prevents releases.
 
•
 
Provide secondary containment when storing hazardous substances in bulk quantities (~55 g
allons
).
 
•
 
Maintain good housekeeping practices for all chemical materials at the facility.
 
2
.4
 
Accident Reporting
 
All accidents will be reported to the site’s Lead Technician, the 
Stellar
 
Field
 
Operations Manager or 
the 
SSSM 
as soon as possible after it occurs. A complete follow
-
up written accident investigation report will be 
submitted to the 
Stellar 
Site Field Technician, 
Stellar
 
Field Operations Manager or SSSM within 24 hours.
 
Accident investigations will be handled by each Subcontractor using its own internal reporting system. A copy 
of this report will be submitted to the 
Stellar Site
 
Superintendent, 
Stellar
 
Manager or SSSM, as described 
above.
 
Accident investigations involving hazardous materials or wastes will be handled jointly by Subcontractor and 
the 
Stellar Site
 
Field Technician, 
Stellar
 
Field Operations Manager or SSSM. This is to 
ensure
 
the cause of the 
accident is determined and proper precautions are implemented for other similar activities. The corrective 
action expected must be relayed to other subcontractors and employees.

2
.12
 
Fall Protection 
 
Fall protection shall be provided on all fixed elevated surfaces above 4 feet for all trades. The 4
-
foot fall 
protection rule does not pertain to ladders and scaffolding as long as they are used within OSHA standards.
 
Subcontractors that work from temporary elevated surface heights of 6 feet or more will be required to 
provide a written fall protection plan. Said plan shall be submitted and approved prior to Subcontractor 
starting any work with a fall risk.
 
All employees shall wear a full body harness and double shock
-
absorbing lanyard system anytime a worker is 
required to disconnect and reconnect to travel around an obstacle. At no time will a worker be totally 
“unhooked”.

.13

Confined space work requiring an entry permit shall be performed only under the supervision of a competent 
trained person. Only trained and authorized employees shall be allowed to enter the confined space. A 
Confined Space Entry Permit is available from 
Red Hills 
Builders. Subcontractors may also use any equivalent

Housekeeping
 
Regular housekeeping is a part of this job safety plan with special emphasis on keeping pathways and 
walkways clean and free of debris. Our current operating assets in unincorporated Navajo County comply with 
local government regulations, such as the Navaj
o County Health Code and the Navajo County Solid Waste 
Ordinance, regarding the cleanliness of both the interior and exterior perimeters, ensuring all areas are kept 
free of trash and debris. Additionally, we strictly adhere to all relevant environmental l
aws and standards, 
including the Clean Water Act (CWA) and the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA), to maintain a 
safe and compliant work environment.
 
2
.15
 
Electrical
 
Please see Section 
2
.1
8
 
for Lockout/Tagout (LOTO)
 
Procedures
 
All 
temporary power sources will be provided with Ground Fault Circuit Interrupters (GFCI), and all cords, 
plugs and receptacles shall be checked for damage daily. Testing of the ground and labeling of the cords will 
be performed as needed or at least monthly.
 
Remove any damaged equipment from use and tag out of service 
until repaired.
 
Tools and equipment shall be routinely inspected for frayed cords, loose wires and plugs and should be tested 
before use.
 
2
.16
 
Forklifts
 
No modifications or additions that affect the capacity or safe operations of the equipment shall be made 
without the 
manufacturer’s
 
written approval. Only trained and certified personnel shall be permitted to 
operate forklifts. All forklifts must be inspected daily before operations begin.
 
If a 
load is lifted by two or more trucks working in unison, the proportion of the total load carried by any one 
truck shall not exceed its capacity.
 
 
2
.17
 
Tools
 
Impact tools, such as drift pins, wedges and chisels shall be kept free of mushroomed heads.
 
The wooden handles of tools shall be kept free of splinters or cracks and shall be kept tight in the tool.
 
 
2
.18
 
Lockout / Tagout 
(LOTO) 
Procedures
 
Before any modifications, maintenance, or repairs are done on equipment, tools, or power panels, the energy 
source shall be disconnected or turned off (turn valve, pull fuse, switch breaker), absence of voltage verified, 
grounded if over 600
 
volts
 
and locked out or blocked out with a padlock, chain or both to ensure energy 
source is locked off.

10
 
1.
 
Place a tag at the disconnect point, identifying who you are, who you work for, and why you locked it 
off. Never move or remove another person’s tag.
 
2.
 
Be sure to release residual energy (i.e. lead line 
grounding circuits
).
 
3.
 
Test equipment or energy source to ensure it will not run. Turn on equipment or test circuits to ensure 
it 
is disconnected
.
 
4.
 
Restore energy safely when you are finished with your repairs. 
 
5.
 
Remove lock and tag.

2
.20
 
Hot Work
 
Subcontractors performing Hot Work such as welding, cutting, brazing, soldering, and grinding are 
exposed to 
the risk of fires from ignition of flammable or combustible materials in the space, and from leaks of flammable 
gas into the space, from Hot Work equipment.
 
All Hot Work performed by any person will require a JHA and written plan review and approval by the 
Stellar 
Site Field Technician prior to the start of the job.
 
A Hot Work permit will be required for any work activity performed in an enclosed environment, including but 
not limited to inside a building or a confined space, that generates sparks, open flames or creates in any way a 
potential fire hazard. 
 
2.21
 
Residual Toxic Chemicals or Contamina
nts
 
on Site
 
Th
e 
project 
area 
has no known contamina
n
t
s
.
 
However, if residual contamination was identified during 
operations, the following steps should be taken
 
in contaminated work zones
: 
 
•
 
Establish a Worker Decontamination Enclosure System or "Regulated Area.” Once set up, this system is 
to be used for all access to and from potentially contaminated areas for personnel and equipment, 
except in an emergency. If an occupied setting, this encl
osure should be reviewed by the SOLV Energy, 
LLC Safety Department to assure proper containment.
 
•
 
Seal off 
openings such as doorways, windows, and ventilation ducts with plastic sheets sealed with
 
tape. Do not block off emergency or fire exits in such a way they cannot be used in an emergency.
 
Place 
OSHA Asbestos approved warning signs at all possible exits.
 
•
 
Maintain all work areas in a clean and orderly manner each day. Treat any material exposed to
 
Asbestos as contaminated. No food, drink, or smoking is allowed in controlled areas.

<!-- page 847 -->
Red Hills Solar and Storage 
Project 
Site
-
Specific 
Safety 
Plan
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
      
 
11
 
•
 
Pre
-
clean and cover fixed objects within work areas with a minimum of 6
-
mil plastic. Remove all 
movable furniture from contamination zones. Cover wall and carpeted surfaces in a manner that allows 
adequate overlapping and tape all joints. It is recommended
 
that wall barriers be constructed of a 
minimum of 6 mil plastic, floor barriers at least two layers of 6 mil or equivalent, and all other areas or 
items can be protected with a minimum of 6 mil plastic to maintain an adequate air seal.
 
•
 
All Asbestos waste will be placed in double bagged 6 mil (minimum) polyethylene bags or lined 
fiberboard drums and properly marked. Disposal containers shall be suitable to receive and retain any 
Asbestos containing materials until disposal at an approved 
site. The containers must be air and 
watertight and labeled in accordance with EPA and Federal OSHA regulations. Note: Bagged asbestos 
waste must be visibly wet inside the containers. A label should be placed inside the second bag and be 
visible for inspec
tions.
 
•
 
Establish, identify and maintain emergency and fire exits from the work areas. Have a written 
emergency plan posted and adequate firefighting equipment available. Be sure all employees are 
trained in these emergency procedures. Do not allow smoking or open
 
flames in 
containment areas
. 
Plastic is very flammable. Post "no smoking" signs at all entry areas.
 
•
 
Inspect negative airflow HEPA filtration ventilation to assure that there is no air movement from
 
containment to non
-
controlled areas. Smoke tests should be conducted daily to assure the
 
ventilation 
system is operating correctly. The containment area shall be maintained 
under negative
 
pressure with a 
minimum of 0.04 inches of water as indicated on a manometer. The
 
abatement contractor shall provide 
DOP test results on the HEPA units if requested.
 
•
 
All workers or visitors entering containment areas must wear appropriate personal protective
 
equipment. All employees shall be trained in the proper use of their protective gear and it's use
 
strictly 
enforced. Protective gear includes such items as Tyvek (paper) coveralls, hoods, booties
 
and dual 
cartridge respirators approved by NIOSH/MESA for asbestos. Each person leaving
 
containment areas 
must follow the routine decontamination process. Disposable items will be
 
treated as Asbestos waste.
 
•
 
All vacuum and air purifying equipment must be supplied with multiple HEPA filtration. This
 
equipment 
shall be maintained according to manufacturer's recommendations. Written
 
maintenance records must 
be kept verifying compliance.
 
•
 
A daily log should be maintained showing all persons entering regulated/contaminated areas. It
 
should 
be verified prior to entry, via badging system or equivalent, that a worker is AHERA trained
 
and 
authorized to enter controlled areas.
 
•
 
Post asbestos warning signs at all entrances to regulated work areas.

3.3
 
Site 
Evacuation Plan / Assembly Area
 
Site evacuation procedures are required as part of an emergency response plan. Upon the plant/site 
handover to the 
Stellar
 
staff, every job site will be evaluated for a safe corridor for escape and assembly. 
Most site assembly areas will be located outside of the main access gate. Examples of emergencies 
requiring a site evacuation include:
 
•
 
Equipment fire or explosion.
 
•
 
Explosion from underground pocket of flammable/combustible gases.
 
•
 
Inclement weather.
 
•
 
Toxic gas/vapor release from subsurface pocket of gases or containers.
 
•
 
Cave
-
in from excavated trenching.
 
During any construction work, evacuation routes are established upwind and a cross from the direction of 
wind flow as determined by either a windsock or other visual means of determining air movement. In the 
event of an evacuation signal, every worker is r
equired to cease operations, note the wind pattern and 
move in a cross and upwind direction to the designated assembly point.
 
An Emergency Assembly Map with a site
-
specific assembly point will be developed closer to construction.
 
3.4 Response to Release of Hazardous Materials/Wastes
 
The project 
area
 
is
 
equipped with spill kits to handle the containment and clean
-
 
up of minor spills. For 
spills over 25 gallons, technicians should attempt to stop the leak (if possible), and contain the spill then 
contact a Lead Field technician immediately. The Lead Field
 
Technician shall evaluate the extent of the 
spill and determine if the local Spill Remediation Contractor needs to be called in for clean
-
up. 
Notifications to the National Response Center (NRC) and State Environmental agency might be required as 
outlined 
in the site’s Spill Prevention and Response Plan. Any notification to a government agency requires 
follow
-
up notification to the owner and 
Stellar’s
 
Compliance Department. A 
U.S. 
E
nvironmental 
P
rotection 
A
gency
 
identification
 
number
 
may 
be required for waste pick
-
up
 
and
 
must be provided by the site owner.

3.5 Fire
 
Alert and immediately evacuate personnel away from the immediate area. Notify 
Stellar Site
 
F
ield

Stellar

p
roject

ite. If necessary,

For small fires
 
(i.e., 
a fire that can be controlled with one 2.5
-
pound

)
, contain and 
extinguish the fire as quickly as possible. For larger fires, immediately

-

,

r

.
 
3.6 Explosions
 
Following an explosion, immediately survey the affected area for injured workers. If the area is safe to 
enter, move the injured to a safe distance. Injured workers will be transported to the nearest emergency 
medical facility.
 
Once injured workers have been moved, immediately evacuate the affected area and gather in the 
designated assembly area outside of the gate access location. If a fire develops, follow emergency 
procedures for fire control and evacuation, as described above
.
 
3.7 Accidents
 
All accidents/incidents shall be reported to the 
Stellar
 
Lead Field Technician, 
Stellar
 
Field Operations 
Manager or the SSSM immediately for investigation and follow
-
 
up. An incident written incident report 
shall be submitted to the 
Stellar Site
 
Field Technician and SSSM within 24 hours. For accidents involving 
personal injury, immediately apply appropriate first aid and transport the injured party to the designated 
medical facility. Never allow the injured employee to transport them. The 
Stellar Site
 
Field
 
Technician will 
summon emergency medical response for injuries requiring emergency medical assistance and ambulance 
transport.
 
3.8 Vehicle Accidents
 
Stop the vehicle as soon as safely possible. Assess the damage to the vehicle and collateral damage to 
equipment and other objects. If injuries are sustained, follow the accident procedures above. Report all 
vehicle accidents to the 
Stellar
 
Site 
Field Technician, 
Stellar
 
Field Operations Manager or 
the 
SSSM 
immediately.
 
A Vehicle Accident Report must be filled out and submitted to the 
Stellar Site
 
Field 
Operations Manager
 
and 
the 
SSSM
.
 
3.9 Equipment Failure or Power Outage
 
Turn off equipment or power. Assess damage and notify the 
Stellar Site
 
Field Technician or 
Stellar
 
Field 
Operations Manager. Wait for further instructions from 
Stellar Site
 
Field Technician, 
Stellar
 
Field

, or SSSM
.
 
3.10 Natural Disaster/Earthquake Checklist
 
1.
 
Shut down all operations/equipment in a safe effective manner
 
2.
 
Check all personnel for injury and follow appropriate procedures
 
3.
 
Inspect all fuel/oil/wastewater tankage and/or containment structures for signs of leakage or 
damage
 
4.
 
Inspect all operational units for proper operations made, and manually check to insure all automatic 
and alarmed features are 
working properly
 
5.
 
Inspect all piping, values, and fixed pumping units for damage
 
6.
 
Re
-
inspect electrical circuits and power supplies for damage
 
7.
 
Report to assembly point and wait further instructions
 
3.11 Exposure Assessment
 
Subcontractors will become familiar with the potential hazards on the job, as described in this SSSP. They 
will train, manage, and provide appropriate measures to protect their employees. Each Subcontractor 
shall provide appropriate tools, (i.e., PPE, equi
pment, environmental exposure monitors) to assess and 
assure that its employees are working in a safe area and manner.
 
3.12 Liaison, Notification Requirement for Incidents, Accidents and Injuries
 
Should any of the events listed above occur, the 
Stellar Site
 
Field Technician, 
Stellar
 
Field Operations 
Manager, and the SSSM shall be contacted immediately. The SSSM will assist Subcontractors in resolving 
the issue and coordinate the preparation of a written report to the 
Stellar
 
Field Operations Manager 
within 24 hours.
 
Stellar
 
Site Field Technician, Stellar Field Operations Manager, 
and the SSSM will determine the 
appropriate reporting and notification procedures involving notification and follow up to local authorities.

4.
3
 
Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) 
Safety
 
As the project includes a large BESS
 
component
, m
aintaining safety protocols and procedures 
will be
 
paramount. The following requirements and practices are implemented to ensure the safe design, 
construction, installation, operation, and maintenance of the BESS at the 
project 
area
.

<!-- page 853 -->
Red Hills Solar and Storage 
Project 
Site
-
Specific 
Safety 
Plan
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
      
 
17
 
All BESS components will be designed, constructed, and installed in accordance with the latest industry 
standards, including but not limited to 
NFPA 855:2022, International Fire Code: 2021 (IFC), National Electric 
Code: 2020 (NEC), National Electric Fire Protection Agency 70E: 2018, and National Electric Safety Code: 2017 
including TIA 2017
-
1 (NESC)
. Any custom
-
engineered components will be sealed by a Professional Engineer 
licensed in Arizona.
 
The Facility will adhere to NFPA 68:2018 and NFPA 69:2019 for the design, construction, inspection, and 
maintenance of BESS fire safety systems. Testing and maintenance of these systems will comply with NFPA 
72:2022.
 
The factors that could 
lead to the failure of the battery system will be analyzed in accordance with 
NFPA 551:2022
.
 
Battery components will be transported in accordance with U.S. Department of Transportation regulations 
and UN 38.3 requirements. Manufacturers will implement ISO 90001 practices to ensure high
-
quality 
production and minimize premature failures.
 
If there is a
 
non
-
battery
 
fire in the BESS area of the project 
area
, 
fire suppression systems used to control 
the fire 
will comply with NFPA 2001:2022, NFPA 2010:2020, or, when those are not applicable, the 
manufacturer’s
 
standards.
 
For detailed procedures on emergency response specific to the BESS system being utilized in the project, 
the "Tesla Emergency Response Guide" will be provided upon request. This document is subject to 
change, and updates will be provided as needed.

A map of 
road networking and access aisles inside the project fence line 
will be developed closer to the 
construction phase
 
and included in Appendix 
D
. 
The internal site access roads will be designed with adequate 
width to accommodate emergency vehicles and will be constructed as all
-
weather roads to ensure reliable 
access for fire department vehicles and other emergency responders at all times.
 
5.2 O&M Building 
Fire Access Features
 
The site plan includes a designated fire response staging area, ensuring that emergency vehicles have 
easy and unobstructed access to the site. This strategically positioned area is crucial for minimizing 
response times and facilitating efficient firefight
ing operations.
 
A water storage tank will be installed adjacent to the O&M building, providing a reliable and readily 
accessible water source in the event of a fire. This tank enhances the overall fire suppression capabilities 
of the 
O&M building
, ensuring quick access to water for firefighting efforts.

Given the increased risk of wildfires during the summer months in Navajo County, special attention will 
be given during that time of the year to 
mitigate risk. Increased risk mitigation includes but is not limited 
to clearing dry brush around panels and the BESS area, along with more frequent equipment checks.

9
. Personnel Roles and Organizational Responsibilities
 
9
.1 Management Team
 
The 
Stellar 
Management Team for the 
p
roject will include the following: Division Manager, O&M Manager, and 
the Owner’s Representative.
 
All inquiries and decisions regarding the 
p
roject should be addressed to the 
Stellar
 
Division Manager, Project 
Manager or Field Operations Manager. The 
Stellar
 
Manager will act as liaison to the Management Team.
 
Please note that these personnel will be selected prior to the project’s construction period
 
and added to the 
SSSP
.

9
.3 
Renewable Energy and Safety Personnel
 
The following roles, although subject to change prior to construction and operations, will be present on the 
project.
 
9
.3.1
 
Field Division Manager
 
The 
Stellar
 
Division Manager is charged with the overall
 
responsibility for the successful implementation of 
field operations and maintenance. The Division Manager responsibilities include, but are
-
not
-
limited
-
to:
 
•
 
Prepare and organize project activities on
-
site.
 
•
 
Review and approve the site
-
specific H&SP.
 
•
 
Provide operational needs, supplies, etc.

21
 
•
 
Coordinate cost controls.
 
9
.3.2
 
Lead Field Technician
 
The 
Stellar
 
Lead Technician coordinates 
with Site
 
Field Technicians, vendors and subcontractor activities on the
 
project
 
area
. The Lead Technician’s responsibilities include
,
 
but are
 
not
 
limited
 
to:
 
•
 
Serve as one of the On
-
site Primary Contacts.
 
•
 
Prepare and organize project activities on
-
site.
 
•
 
Supervise vendors and subcontractors for compliance with job scope and 
quality.
 
•
 
Supervise field operations and implement safety procedures.
 
•
 
Enforce implementation of SSSP and established health and safety practices.
 
9.3.3
 
Site Technician
 
The 
Stellar 
Site Technician is responsible for supporting field operations and maintenance activities. The Site 
Technician's responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
 
•
 
Summon emergency medical response for injuries requiring emergency medical assistance and 
ambulance transport.
 
•
 
Be notified immediately following vehicle accidents and submit a Vehicle Accident Report.
 
•
 
Be informed of any equipment failure or power outage and provide further instructions.
 
•
 
Conduct damage assessments and provide further instructions post
-
natural disaster or earthquake.
 
9.3.
4
 
Remote Operations Control 
(ROC) C
enter
 
The 
ROC Center
 
is responsible 
for 
overseeing the operational integrity and performance of 
the facility. 
Specifically, duties of the 
ROC Center
 
include but are
-
not
-
limited
-
to:
 
•
 
Ensuring compliance with all 
cybersecurity and operational standards of a NERC Medium
-
Impact 
facility.
 
•
 
Coordinating real
-
time responses to operational issues and emergencies.
 
•
 
Maintaining continuous oversight of facility performance and security.
 
•
 
Supporting field technicians with operational data and troubleshooting guidance
.
 
9
.3.
5
 
Site Specific Safety Manager (SSSM)
 
The SSSM is responsible for assuring compliance with the SSSP. Specifically, duties of the SSSM include but are
-
not
-
limited
-
to:
 
•
 
Establish site safety controls.
 
•
 
Develop the SSSP.
 
•
 
Serve as s
afety 
liaison with vendors and subcontractors on the site.
 
•
 
Serve as the p
oint 
person for health and safety questions.
 
•
 
Monitor 
Red Hills 
personnel, vendor and 
subcontractor compliance
.
 
•
 
Oversee security compliance for the 
Red Hills 
Project.

Red Hills Solar and Storage Project Visual Simulations 
1 
VISUAL SIMULATIONS 
Project Description 
This technical memorandum was prepared to support the Navajo County Special Use Permit process for 
the proposed Red Hills Solar and Storage Project (the project). The visual simulations presented here are 
provided to support the entitlement efforts for the project in unincorporated Navajo County, Arizona. The 
project is approximately 3.5 miles north of the town of Snowflake and approximately 0.5-mile west of 
Arizona State Route (SR) 77. The project area would include construction of a 1,000-megawatt (MW), 
utility-scale photovoltaic solar energy generation facility on approximately 9,090 acres of privately 
owned land and 123 acres of Arizona State Trust Land (project area). Additional project features 
include a 4,000-MW-per-hour battery energy storage system (BESS), a 920-foot-long, 500-kilovolt 
generation-tie transmission line connecting the project substation to the existing Salt River Project 
Sugarloaf substation located within the project area, an operations and maintenance building, and other 
ancillary facilities. The proposed solar panels would be 9 feet 1 inch at maximum height with a 60-degree 
tracking angle. The BESS unit height would be 10 feet with an additional 1-foot foundation. There would 
be two 60-foot-tall monopoles connecting the project substation to the existing Salt River Project 
Sugarloaf substation and a 7-foot-tall, meshed fence with barbed wire surrounding the project area, 
defined as the boundary of the project facilities.  
The visual simulations presented in this memorandum combine three-dimensional computer-generated 
images of the proposed project components with photographs taken from selected key observation points 
(KOPs). The simulations are based on project specifications identified in the project’s preliminary layout 
plan dated May 6, 2024, provided by Stellar Red Hills Solar LLC (Stellar). The simulations depict how 
the project and other related electrical infrastructure would appear from the representative KOPs in the 
surrounding community. 
Summary of Process and Methods 
Field review of the project site and vicinity was conducted by SWCA on April 9, 2024, to identify KOP 
locations and to take photographs from each KOP for the creation of visual simulations. Field evaluation 
was conducted both on foot and from a moving vehicle along public transportation routes. SWCA 
Environmental Consultants (SWCA) coordinated with Stellar to identify four KOPs, selecting areas that 
represent public views near the project (Table 1, Figure 1). 
Table 1. Key Observation Point and Visual Simulation Locations 
KOP Visual Simulation Number Location Description Latitude and Longitude 
KOP 1 SR 77 looking southwest 34.657325, -110.09925 
KOP 2 SR 77 looking west 34.605658, -110.089365 
KOP 3 Riggs Street looking northwest 34.572444, -110.096715 
KOP 4 Four Mile Knoll looking northwest 34.558939, -110.11636 
SWCA personnel used a full-frame, single-lens reflex camera with a fixed 50-millimeter lens to take base 
photographs of the project area under clear weather conditions from GPS points recorded at each KOP. 
Using ArcGIS, Google Earth Pro, Autodesk products (AutoCAD and 3ds Max), and Adobe Photoshop, 
SWCA created a three-dimensional model of the proposed layout of the project. The project model was 
then superimposed on a digital elevation model representing the project area terrain, and digital cameras 
within the software were established at the KOP locations, giving the correct scale, orientation, and

<!-- page 869 -->
Red Hills Solar and Storage Project Visual Simulations 
2 
distance. Date and time-of-day inputs allowed for the application of shadows and reflected light, and the 
software accounted for distance and haze to increase the accuracy of viewing conditions at the time the 
base photographs were taken. The rendered images of the project were then merged into the baseline 
photographs using Adobe Photoshop software. These merged images provide photorealistic simulations 
of the project as viewed from each selected KOP (see Appendix A). Photographs of the existing baseline 
conditions are included for purposes of comparison to proposed visual changes. 
A visual contrast analysis is an established industry method, created by the Bureau of Land Management 
(BLM), of evaluating the anticipated level of change (contrast) associated with the construction, 
operation, and maintenance of a proposed project. Factors taken into consideration for such an analysis 
include the level of perceived contrast between the proposed project elements and the existing landscape 
and the distance of the proposed project elements from the viewer. This analysis informed both the 
assessment of impacts on landscape character and impacts on views from each KOP location.  
The level of perceived contrast between the proposed project elements and the existing landscape is 
classified using the following definitions (BLM 1984): 
• None: The project is not visible or perceived. 
• Weak: The project can be seen but does not attract attention. 
• Moderate: The project somewhat attracts attention and begins to dominate the landscape. 
• Strong: The project demands attention, would not be overlooked, and is dominant in the 
landscape. 
KOP 1 Analysis 
KOP 1 is along SR 77, looking southwest toward the project area. This KOP represents a travel route user 
(i.e., motorists) and is approximately 2.2 miles from the nearest solar array. Views from KOP 1 include 
shallowly undulating rolling terrain with dispersed dark and bright green desert grasses and shrubs, 
uniform geometric barbed-wire fencing, large wind turbines from the Poseidon Wind Project, and lattice 
transmission structures that draw the attention of the viewer. Given the viewing position and proximity to 
the project from KOP 1, the project would not attract attention nor dominate the landscape. The project 
would not demand the attention of the viewer or introduce elements and patterns that would be visually 
dominant. The project would produce weak to no visual contrast, with the effect lasting for a short 
duration based on travel speed along the highway of approximately 65 miles per hour, based on the posted 
speed limit. The project would be intermittently visible, based on screening associated with existing 
topography and vegetation, for travelers heading northbound or southbound along SR 77 for 
approximately 10 minutes along an approximate 11-mile portion of SR 77.  
KOP 2 Analysis 
KOP 2 is also along SR 77, looking west toward the project area. This KOP represents a travel route user 
and is approximately 0.5 mile from the nearest solar array. Views from this KOP include undulating 
rolling terrain with dispersed dark and bright green desert grasses and shrubs leading to tall buttes, 
uniform geometric barbed-wire fencing and gate, and tall wind turbines that draw the attention of the 
viewer. Given the viewing position and proximity to the project from KOP 2, as well as the lack of 
intervening vegetation or topography, the project would attract attention and begin to dominate the 
landscape through the introduction of new forms, lines, colors, and textures resulting from the dark blue 
to grey rectangular solar arrays. The project would begin to demand the attention of the viewer and 
introduce elements and patterns that would be visually dominant. The solar arrays would demand the 
attention of the viewer and introduce elements and patterns that would be visually dominant and create

<!-- page 870 -->
Red Hills Solar and Storage Project Visual Simulations 
3 
strong contrast compared to other features in the landscape over a short duration of view based on the 
posted travel speed of SR 77. The project would be intermittently visible, based on screening associated 
with existing topography and vegetation, for travelers heading northbound or southbound along SR 77 for 
approximately 10 minutes along an approximate 11-mile portion of SR 77.

Red Hills Solar and Storage Project Visual Simulations 
5 
KOP 3 Analysis 
KOP 3 is on Riggs Steet, looking northwest toward the project area. This KOP represents a rural 
residential viewer and is approximately 2.2 miles from the nearest solar array. Views from this KOP 
include undulating rolling terrain with dispersed dark and bright green desert grasses and shrubs, uniform 
geometric barbed-wire fencing paralleling tan dirt roads, wind turbines, and lattice and wooden monopole 
transmission structures. Views also include abandoned buildings and debris in the foreground that draw 
the attention of the viewer, with occupied large rectangular buildings farther in distance. Given this 
KOP’s viewing position, the project would begin to attract attention and begin to dominate the landscape 
through the introduction of new forms, lines, colors, and textures in the form of dark blue to subdued grey 
geometric solar panels. The project infrastructure, including the BESS, interconnection, and substation, 
would begin to draw the attention of the viewer and introduce elements and patterns that would be 
visually dominant. Given the presence of other structures and landscape modifications in view, the project 
would produce a moderate to strong level of contrast with these impacts occurring over a long duration of 
view due to the residential setting. 
KOP 4 Analysis 
KOP 4 is near Four Mile Knoll, looking northwest toward the project area, and is within lands owned by 
the BLM. This KOP represents a recreational user approximately 2.2 miles from the nearest solar array. 
Views from this KOP include shallowly undulating terrain with dispersed dark and bright green desert 
grasses and shrubs leading to tall buttes in the background, uniform geometric barbed-wire fencing, 
wooden monopole transmission structures, and several tall wind turbines in the distance that draw the 
attention of the viewer. Given the viewing position afforded from the top of Four Mile Knoll, which rises 
approximately 140 feet above the adjacent terrain, the project would begin to attract attention and begin to 
dominate the landscape through the introduction of new forms, lines, colors, and textures. The project 
would begin to demand the attention of the viewer and introduce elements and patterns that would be 
visually dominant. Given the presence of other structures and landscape modifications in view, the project 
would produce a moderate to strong level of contrast, with these impacts anticipated to be of moderate 
duration, given that recreators tend to spend time taking in the view from the high point of a landscape 
feature like Four Mile Knoll.

INSTRUCTIONS FOR PETITION FOR REVIEW OF NOTICE OF CHANGE
lnformation necessary to complete this petition is contained on the Notice of Change. Additional information
regarding your property value or classification may be obtained from the County Assessor of the county in
which the property is located.
. The following forms may need to be used in conjunction with the Petition for Review (DOR form 82130NC) in
the administrative appeals process and can be obtained from your local County Assessor:
1 . Agency Authorization form (DOR 82130AA)
2. Appropriate lncome and Expense Statement from the DOR 82300 series.
3. Multiple Parcel Appeal form (DOR 82131 )
4. Agricultural Land Use Application (DOR 82916)

such as copies of your .Driver License .Voter Registration Card .Copy of a portion of your last lncome Tax
Retum (only name and address section) in addition to Utility bill or Motor Vehicle Registration.
lf you are appealing to obtain qualified agricultural classification, provide the Assessor with a compleled
Agricultural Land Use Application form (DOR 82916) together with substantial information iustirying your appeal.
Keep a copy of all information that is submitted to the Assessor.
MULTIPLE PARCEL APPEAL
. You may flle an appeal for more than one parcel if all of the parcels are one of the following:
1. Part of the same economic unit. An "Economic Unit" is a combination of parcels in which land and
improvements are used for mutual economic benefit. An economic unit may be comprised of properties which
are neither contiguous nor owned by the same owner. However, they must be managed and operated on a
unitary basis and each parcel must make a functional contribution to the operation ofthe unit. "Functional
Contribution" is a positive economic benefit created by the use of an individual parcel in an economic unit.
2. Owned by the same owner, have the same use, have the same appeal basis, and are located in the
same geographic area. Criteria for determination of "Same Use" includes, but is not limited to, property
class, property use code, unit value, and zoning. "Geographic Area" means an area for which common
property valuation characteristics may reasonably be identified, such as a subdivision, neighborhood,
market area, or an Assessor's book and map.
. lt is strongly recommended that only parcels with common ownership, physical characteristics and
location be included on a Multiple Parcel Appeal form (DOR 82131). Failure to file multiple parcels under the
above conditions could result in a decision based on incomplete information or a possible denial of the appeal.
ln ltems 8 and 9 of the petition form, enter the total full cash and limited values for all parcels included in the
appeal.
